payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Make her close her jacket fully
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Is the woman's jacket fully closed?
node.criteria: Use only the evidence in s1 and s2 for the requested jacket change. Complete if s2 passes. Partial if s2 does not pass, s1 passes, and the evidence establishes some progress toward closing the jacket. Absent if both checks fail and the evidence establishes no requested progress. Unknown if required evidence is unresolved such that complete, partial, or absent cannot be determined. Unrelated edits do not count as progress; do not treat unknown evidence as failure or completion.
node.binding: Target: The jacket is fully closed, with its front panels brought together and no visible opening remaining along the closure.. Reference: The woman's jacket in the input image..

node_traces.evidence: Both saved checks fail: s2 reports the jacket remains visibly open, and s1 reports it is not more closed than in the source. The evidence establishes no progress toward the requested change.

dependencies.evidence: The jacket’s front is visibly more open in the edited image: a panel hangs away from her body rather than the front panels being brought together as in the source. It is not closed more than in the input.
The edited image shows the jacket hanging open, with a large visible gap between its front panels; it is not fully closed.

The jacket’s front is visibly more open in the edited image: a panel hangs away from her body rather than the front panels being brought together as in the source. It is not closed more than in the input.

response.content: {"text":"The node’s criterion and binding already capture the requested end state, and the traces are valid, queried, and high-confidence; there is no transport, schema, or dependency failure to repair. The edited image appears to show the jacket hanging open, while the source is too distant to establish a clear closure baseline. However, the reference label is an aggregate constraint, not atomic proof that the jacket is closed. Investigate the disagreement rather than changing the criterion or forcing “yes”: verify that s1 and s2 compare the same jacket and relevant front closure, and that s2 assesses the edited image directly rather than inheriting s1’s conclusion. Ask for observable evidence of the front panels and any remaining opening, and distinguish a genuinely visible open gap from occlusion or an unclear view. If the checks remain valid and the gap is clearly visible, retain the negative visual finding; do not infer progress or completion from the reference label alone."}
